title: Global identifiability of a behavioral SIR model for every integer saturation exponent k >= 2
description: Article (version 1.1) with exact-check code. For the behavioral SIR model S' = -beta S I/(1+alpha I)^k, I' = beta S I/(1+alpha I)^k - gamma I, R' = gamma I, observed through I(t) with known total population, the article proves global structural identifiability for every fixed integer k >= 2 (Conjecture 2 of Pant, Saucedo and Pogudin, integer case). The proof combines a closed form of the minimal input-output equation and an explicit rational inverse of its coefficients with a lemma that the reduced two-state model has no nonconstant rational first integral, and uses results of Ovchinnikov, Pogudin and Thompson. The proof is in prose; it is not formalized in a proof assistant and has not undergone human expert review. Exact computer-algebra checks for finitely many k accompany it. Non-integer or unknown k and estimation from noisy data are not covered. Text and data: CC BY 4.0; code: Apache 2.0.
